_comment: Manifest for the Phase-4a ranking-evals corpus. Maps each resume fixture
id (== filename stem under fixtures/resumes/) to its expected ranking tag.
Kept deliberately separate from the resume fixtures themselves so a coder
can't quietly relabel a fixture to make a metric pass.
Tags: 'strong' / 'borderline' / 'weak' / 'adversarial'.
- strong / borderline: expected to surface in the top-k shortlist.
- weak: honestly lacks most required skills; must NOT surface in top-k.
- adversarial: a keyword-stuffer that lists every required/nice-to-have
skill by name but whose cited chunks carry no real supporting text
for those claims (see 'adversarial_type'). A correct anti-fabrication
evidence verifier (>= MatchWeights.evidence_verify_fuzz against the
cited chunk) must fail to verify these quotes, so this resume must
NOT surface in top-k even though its keyword overlap with the JD is
the highest of the whole corpus.
JDExtracted has no 'seniority' or per-skill 'is_must_have' field (see
core/src/schemas/jobs.py): every entry in the JD's required_skills is an
implicit must-have for stage-2 structured skill scoring; entries in
nice_to_have_skills feed stage-3 evidence text only, per the
'NICE_TO_HAVE skills' decision recorded in docs/EXTRACTION_PLAN.md.
--- Phase-4a strengthening additions (adequacy-review round 1) ---
must_not_surface_in_topk: true on every 'weak'/'adversarial' entry -- the
backstop the ranking-evals gate enforces against thresholds.toml's
[adversarial].must_not_surface_in_topk / [evidence].min_completeness_in_topk
once Phase 4c lands (see docs/adr for the invariant). NOT computed here.
expected_rank_band: {min, max} the tag implies for a CORRECT ranker's
output order (max=null means unbounded / 'anywhere below the top tier').
Bands are per-TAG canonical ranges (every 'strong' entry shares the same
band) and are strictly ordered/disjoint across tiers. See the round-2
note below for how the concrete numbers are derived.
gold_evidence: for a couple of 'strong' fixtures, skill.name -> the EXACT
substring of that skill's cited chunk text a correct evidence verifier
should quote. 4c's fuzz-boundary test perturbs these toward ~0.83
(must fail >= evidence_verify_fuzz) and ~0.87 (must pass). Fixture-only;
no scoring logic here.
--- Phase-4a strengthening additions (round 2: GAP 1 + GAP 2) ---
GAP 1 fix (expected_rank_band feasibility): a band is only useful if a
CORRECT ranker can actually satisfy it. Bands are now computed FROM the
corpus's tier population counts so they are feasible BY CONSTRUCTION and
tile ranks 1..N with no gap/overlap, walked in ascending-rank order:
strong -> [1, Nstrong], borderline -> [Nstrong+1, Nstrong+Nborderline],
weak/adversarial (share one band) -> [Nstrong+Nborderline+1, null].
With the current corpus (7 strong, 4 borderline, 4 weak, 1 adversarial)
that's strong [1,7] < borderline [8,11] < weak/adversarial [12,null].
`core/tests/unit/test_evals_corpus.py::test_expected_rank_bands_fit_tier_
populations` re-derives the required window widths from the ACTUAL tag
populations on every run and fails if a band is too narrow for its tier
(this is exactly the bug that shipped in round 1: expected_rank_band
[1,3] for 'strong' while the corpus had 5 'strong' fixtures -- no
correct ranker could ever satisfy that). Whenever a fixture's tag
changes, recompute every band below.
GAP 2 fix (matched-pair 'ordering_controls'): r11 (education), r13
(overqual), and r04 (motivation) each only moved score WITHIN a tier,
so a ranker that ignored those dimensions still passed every invariant.
r14/r15/r16 are TWIN fixtures -- each identical to its partner in every
scoring-relevant field (skills/chunks/experience/years) EXCEPT the one
target dimension -- so that dimension is the SOLE differentiator between
the pair. `ordering_controls` below records, per pair, which member a
correct ranker must place strictly higher and why. The pairwise
rank(higher) < rank(lower) ASSERTION itself is a Phase-4c test (needs
the live ranker); Phase 4a only guarantees the twins are genuinely
'identical except X' via the per-pair integrity tests in
test_evals_corpus.py, which is the thing that makes the eventual 4c
assertion trustworthy rather than confounded.

gold_evidence.Python: Designed and shipped Python REST APIs consumed by 40+ internal services
gold_evidence.PostgreSQL: Optimized PostgreSQL schemas and queries, cutting p95 latency 35% across core tables

gold_evidence.Apache Airflow: Authored and maintained 30+ Apache Airflow DAGs covering ingestion, transformation, and reporting jobs
gold_evidence.Docker: Introduced Kafka topics for near-real-time event ingestion and packaged consumers with Docker

ordering_controls.rationale: r14 and r11 are identical in skills, cited chunks, experience, and total_years_experience. r14 holds a CS/allowed-field (Computer Science) bachelor's degree; r11 holds an otherwise-equivalent bachelor's in a non-allowed field (Mechanical Engineering). MatchWeights.education_partial (0.5) should demote r11 relative to r14 -- education is otherwise a same-tier, within-tier signal that a dimension-blind ranker could ignore without failing any tier-level invariant.

r15 and r13 are identical in skills, cited chunks, experience, and education. r15's total_years_experience=6 gives ratio 6/5=1.2 (< MatchWeights.overqual_ratio=2.0), so it is NOT overqualified; r13's total_years_experience=14 gives ratio 14/5=2.8 (>= overqual_ratio), triggering the overqual penalty (slope/floor). A dimension-blind ranker would score both identically since every other field matches.

r04 and r16 are identical in skills, cited chunks, experience, education, and total_years_experience. r04 carries non-empty cover_letter_chunks (genuine motivation/role-alignment evidence); r16 has NO cover letter at all. MatchWeights.motivation (0.1 top-level weight) should rank r04 strictly above r16 -- previously r04 was the corpus's ONLY cover-letter fixture, so motivation had no second candidate to be ranked against and could not be gated at all.
